parts.refutation: Two requirement checks fail. They fail in the specification and the firmware, not in the silicon. 'watchdog window (V1, V2)': the window is empty. The longest legitimate stall found is 900 ms (V2), and the stop deadline found is 200 ms (V1). No timeout is above 900 ms and at most 200 ms. The 400 ms packaged-part sector erase alone exceeds 200 ms. The silicon's range is not the limit: LOAD is 24 bits, 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds' (RP2350 datasheet build 2025-07-29, section 12.9). 'image watchdog timeout (V4)': the image sets no timeout. There is no watchdog call under firmware/iomcu/ at c25aa86; the word appears only in comments at main.c:970-973. Every other datasheet value re-read passes. The RP2354B is a fixed input: by Research.md:42-43 it is reported to the owner, not re-selected.

figures.evidence: pico-sdk stdio_usb.c is byte-identical in 2.3.0 and 2.3.1. stdio_usb_out_chars is at lines 102-132. It loops while the host takes nothing, until time_us_64() > last_avail_time + PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US. last_avail_time is set on each write into the CDC FIFO. stdio_usb.h:31-33 sets the default to 500000. Nothing under firmware/ overrides it. main.c:1049-1087 holds one window per pass. out_store_tick either erases (out_store.c:337, returns OUT_STORE_ERASED) or programs (:352, OUT_STORE_WROTE). The reclaim erase (:376) runs only when the tick was IDLE, so a pass never has both. A printf follows each window, and can_report follows at main.c:1089. The boot loop at main.c:937-942 runs up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 (out_store.h:122) erases, each with a printf. W25Q16JV-DTR Rev I (published 2026-05-28): tSE 45 ms typ and 400 ms max; tPP 0.4 ms typ and 3 ms max. So one pass is at most 400 ms + 500 ms = 900 ms with a host that stops reading, and an accepted write restarts the 500 ms.
figures.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/pico-sdk/2.3.0/src/rp2_common/pico_stdio_usb/stdio_usb.c and /2.3.1/ (same), .../include/pico/stdio_usb.h; firmware/iomcu/src/main.c, out_store.c, out_store.h, CMakeLists.txt:98-99 at c25aa86; https://www.winbond.com/resource-files/W25Q16JV_DTR%20RevI%2005252026%20Plus.pdf (SHA-256 1aaae1ed...8e18), AC table

figures.evidence: On master, rp2350.cfg has CPUTAPID 0x00040927, an ADIv6 DAP, and Cortex-M33 cores at AP 0x2000 and 0x4000. It defaults USE_CORE to { cm0 cm1 }, so RISC-V and SBA are not selected by default. It defines 'flash bank $_FLASHNAME rp2xxx 0x10000000 $_FLASHSIZE ...', with _FLASHNAME = $_CHIPNAME.flash and FLASHSIZE 0 meaning detect. rp2xxx.c calls the ROM's connect_internal_flash, flash_range_erase and flash_range_program. It reads the JEDEC ID and falls back to SFDP when bank->size is 0. spi.c:132-133 lists 'win w25q16jv' 0x001540ef and 0x001570ef at 0x200000. The latest rp2xxx.c commit is 2025-06-29. One addition: rp2350.cfg has a later commit, a2c6d1522d of 2026-09-06 ('Use -tap instead of -chain-position'), so the master cfg read is newer than the bench's 2026-02-16 snapshot. The flash-bank lines are unchanged, and the conclusion holds.

Section 12.9: LOAD maximum 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds'; the tick comes from the ticks block (12.9.2). The listing of _watchdog_enable (12.9.6.1) clamps load_value to WATCHDOG_LOAD_BITS and sets or clears the PAUSE_DBG0/DBG1/JTAG bits. V1 (200 ms), V2 (900 ms) and V4 (none) are re-read above. 900 > 200 and 400 > 200, so no timeout fits.

figures.figure: re-rank report: VBUS54CV-HSF steering to VBUS
figures.evidence: Application note, word for word: 'An avalanche diode clamps the supply line (VBUS at pin 5) to ground (pin 2). The high speed data lines ... are connected to pin 1, 3, 4 and 6. As long as the signal voltage on the data lines is between the ground- and the VBUS -level, the low capacitance PN-diodes offer a very high isolation'. So a data line held above an absent VBUS forward-biases a steering diode. The datasheet states no figure for that current.

Holding Voltage VH 5.5 V min; Trigger Voltage VTRIG 9.5 V max; VBR 6 V min at IR 1 mA; Operating Voltage (DC) VDC 6 V. The word 'snapback' is not in the text, but VH below VTRIG describes that behaviour.

figures.evidence: IP4234CZ6 Rev. 3.0 (31 January 2018): Vesd +/-15 kV, 'all pins; IEC 61000-4-2 level 4; contact discharge'. The features give '+/-8 kV contact discharge'. No air-discharge figure appears. PRTR5V0U2F Rev. 02 (19 February 2009): VESD 8 kV (IEC 61000-4-2, contact discharge), '> 8 kV (contact)'. No air figure appears. Both datasheets say 'level 4' but specify contact only.

The list omits values that IOBoard.md sets for the microcontroller. First, '520 kB SRAM on the die' (IOBoard.md:53 and :103; Research.md:47). The list keeps the 48 GPIO, the 8 ADC inputs and the absence of PSRAM from the same line, but not the SRAM. The RP2350 datasheet gives 520 kB (lines at section 2 / Table of features: '520 kB on-chip SRAM'), so the value passes, but it is not listed. Second, the pad input leakage of 1 uA with no IOVDD condition, which IOBoard.md:105 cites and the R1 row asks R1 to confirm. Also not carried as requirements: the pin assignments IOBoard.md relies on, QSPI_SS pin 75 and RUN pin 35 (BOOT and RESET line). The V1, V2, V4 and V7 entries are no weaker than their answers.
